title: Skills, transport and learning from failure

tasks.prompt: Describe a skill that you learned outside a classroom, such as cooking, a sport, an instrument or a tool. How did you learn it, and what made it hard or easy? Include specific details.
tasks.follow_up: Many people believe that skills we teach ourselves stay with us longer than skills we learn in class. How does your experience support or challenge this view? Explain with details.

conversation.speaker: professor
conversation.text: Come in. Oh, hi Maya. What can I do for you?

conversation.speaker: student
conversation.text: Hi, Professor Lee. I wanted to ask about the lab report that's due on Friday.

conversation.speaker: professor
conversation.text: Sure. Is something wrong with your data?

conversation.speaker: student
conversation.text: Not exactly. Our sensor stopped working halfway through the experiment, so we only have about half of the measurements.

conversation.speaker: professor
conversation.text: I see. That happens more often than you'd think. Did you tell the lab technician?

conversation.speaker: student
conversation.text: Yes. He fixed it yesterday, but the lab is fully booked until next Tuesday.

conversation.speaker: professor
conversation.text: Okay, here's what I suggest. Write up the results you have, and explain clearly what went wrong. Then repeat the missing runs on Tuesday and add them as an appendix.

conversation.speaker: student
conversation.text: So we can still hand in the main report on Friday?

conversation.speaker: professor
conversation.text: Yes. And I'll give you until next Thursday for the appendix. Just mention our conversation in your cover note.

conversation.speaker: student
conversation.text: That's really helpful. Thank you so much.

tasks.prompt: Some universities require every student to take courses outside their main subject. Do you think this is a good policy? Give reasons and examples for your answer.
Talk about a time when you had to explain something difficult to a person who knew little about the topic.
bullets: How did you make it clear?
How did the other person react?

questions: I'd like to ask you a few questions about public transport. How do most people in your city get to work or to school?
I see. Here's another question. What would make more people choose buses or trains instead of cars?
Interesting. Do you think public transport should be free for everyone? Why or why not?
Thanks for talking about transport with me. Now I'd like to change topics and ask you about online courses. Have you ever taken a course online, and what was it like?
I see. What do students lose when a class moves fully online?
Thanks. One last question. How do you think universities will teach students twenty years from now?

tasks.prompt: Some people say that we learn more from failure than from success. Describe a failure that taught you something. What happened, what did you learn, and how does it change what you do now?
